title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck works in functorial algebraic geometry. He takes the topos \hat C_k of functors from the category C_k of k-algebras to Ens, i.e. presheaves on affine k-schemes.

Step 1. The forgetful functor A ↦ A is an object of \hat C_k with a k-algebra structure; this is the affine line, denoted O_k.

Step 2. For a k-module M, set V(M)(A) = Hom_{k-mod}(M,A) = Hom_{A-mod}(M_A, A). This is an O_k-module, the 'vector bundle' functor V(M) = Spec Sym*(M). It is contravariant in M.

Step 3. He claims V is fully faithful from k-modules to O_k-Modules: Hom_k(M,N) ≅ Hom_{O_k}(V(N),V(M)).

Step 4. To analyse arbitrary (non-linear) morphisms of functors he uses Yoneda. V(N) is represented by Sym*(N), so Hom_{\hat C_k}(V(N),F) ≅ F(Sym*N). For F = Spec B this is Hom_{k-alg}(B, Sym*N). For B = Sym*(M) it gives Hom_{\hat C_k}(V(N),V(M)) ≅ Hom_{k-mod}(M, Sym*N).

Step 5. A morphism u*: V(N) → V(M) corresponds to u: M → Sym*N. He decomposes u = Σ u_i with u_i: M → Sym^i N, a locally finite family (for each x only finitely many u_i(x) ≠ 0).

Step 6 (continued on the next page). For λ ∈ A, the homothety λ on V(N) corresponds to u ↦ Σ λ^i u_i. Hence u* is homogeneous of degree n (u*∘λ = λ^n∘u*) iff u lands in Sym^n N. The proof takes A = k[T] and λ = T. In particular, O_k-linear maps (n = 1) are exactly the k-linear maps M → N, which recovers full faithfulness.

Purpose. This is the preliminary 'yoga' relating coalgebras/polynomial maps to algebras. It sets up the dictionary between homogeneous polynomial maps of functors and graded pieces of Sym, presumably to be dualised to divided powers Γ (Roby's polynomial laws) for the divided-power de Rham complex.
errors: No mathematical error. Full faithfulness holds without finiteness hypotheses on M, N. It needs no separate argument, because O_k-linearity forces homogeneity of degree 1, hence u: M → N; additivity is then automatic. The page asserts it before proving it, and the justification comes on the next page.
'Locally finite' is the right notion: an arbitrary map u: M → Sym*N decomposes into graded components with finitely many nonzero for each x, but not uniformly in x.

ideas.what: Functor of points / topos of functors on k-algebras, with O_k the affine line as ring object
ideas.modern_name: Functorial algebraic geometry (fpqc/big presheaf topos, Demazure–Gabriel style)

ideas.what: V(M) = Spec Sym M as O_k-module, V fully faithful (contravariant) from k-modules to O_k-modules
ideas.modern_name: Vector bundle functor W(M)/V(M); full faithfulness of the module-to-O-module functor

ideas.what: Morphisms of functors V(N) → V(M) ↔ Hom(M, Sym N); homogeneous degree n ↔ M → Sym^n N (test with A = k[T], λ = T)
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial laws / homogeneous polynomial maps (dual form of Roby's theorem with Γ^n)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard Yoneda-based setup of polynomial/homogeneous maps between vector-bundle functors, well known from Roby and SGA 3. It is only preliminary to the divided-power de Rham material.
